text: The named coordinate-ring map is exactly the canonical algebra map p↦p/1 into the determinant localization. Its construction through the scalar tower does not introduce a different function. This matches the localization map in [Stacks, localization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CM), over any commutative base ring; the equation itself asserts no injectivity or cancellation property. Checks pass: [localizedGenericMatrix_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L90), [comul_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L163).
Localized matrix entries use precisely this canonical map.
The explicit map has the expected compatibility with comultiplication.

The localized generic matrix has (i,j)-entry equal to the image of the polynomial variable xᵢⱼ. Entrywise application of the canonical localization map yields this directly, fixing the indices and their order. It is the universal matrix of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51); no transposition or choice of basis is hidden in the definition. Checks pass: [genericMatrix_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L495), [pointToGeneralLinear_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L77).
The bundled generic matrix retains the same indexed coordinate.
Point evaluation reads precisely that matrix entry.

On every polynomial coordinate, the localized coproduct equals the matrix-monoid coproduct followed by localization in both tensor factors. This is the restriction property of the localization lift, and retains the multiplication formula in [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). The equality is between actual images of polynomials; it requires neither injectivity of localization nor injectivity of the tensor-factor maps. Checks pass: [comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L220), [comul_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L277).
The restriction gives the ordered matrix-product formula on generators.
The localized determinant has the required tensor-square image.

The counit on the determinant localization restricts to identity-matrix evaluation on the original polynomial ring. The lift exists because that evaluation sends the determinant to one, hence to a unit. Thus the formula expresses the identity-point map of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51) without requiring the polynomial-to-localization map to be injective. Checks pass: [counit_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L230), [counit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L294).
The restriction evaluates coordinates as identity-matrix entries.
The inverted determinant evaluates to one.

For every polynomial coordinate, the antipode evaluates that polynomial at the entries of the inverse localized generic matrix, as in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). Localization proves the determinant is a unit, so Lean’s totalized matrix inverse is a genuine inverse here. The formula concerns the polynomial image and uses no cancellation through the localization map. Checks pass: [antipode_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L238), [antipode_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L300).
Individual variables evaluate to the matching inverse entries.
The determinant evaluates to its genuine ring inverse.

The coproduct of xᵢⱼ is ∑ₖxᵢₖ⊗xₖⱼ, exactly the coordinate formula for multiplying two matrices in that order from [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). All indices range over Fin n, hence exactly n entries. Evaluating the two tensor factors at points produces their ordinary matrix product; there is no transpose or opposite-group convention. Checks pass: [map_comul_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L247), [pointToGeneralLinear_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L183).
The generator formulas assemble into the product of tensor-factor matrices.
Point evaluation carries this coproduct to ordinary multiplication.

The counit sends a diagonal coordinate to one and an off-diagonal coordinate to zero. These are precisely the entries of the identity matrix, so this is the identity-point evaluation in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). The formula is over the original commutative ring R; zero rings and rank zero require no additional exception. Checks pass: [map_counit_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L261), [coordinateHopfAlgebra_counit_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L613).
The entry equations assemble into the identity matrix.
The selected bundled counit retains the same entry values.

The antipode sends xᵢⱼ to the (i,j)-entry of the inverse generic matrix, matching [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). The indices are unchanged; the adjugate construction already supplies the necessary transpose of cofactors internally. Although matrix inversion is defined at noninvertible matrices in Lean, the localized determinant is a unit, so this value is the actual inverse entry. Checks pass: [map_antipode_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L268), [isUnit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L113).
The entry equations assemble into the full inverse matrix.
The determinant is a unit, guaranteeing a genuine inverse.

Applying the coproduct to the localized matrix entrywise gives the product of its left and right tensor copies, in that order. Matrix multiplication expands to the coproduct sums in [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). The tensor-factor maps are canonical algebra homomorphisms; this identity does not assume they embed their source rings injectively. Checks pass: [comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L220), [comul_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L277).
Every entry has the matrix-product sum.
Taking determinants gives the tensor-square formula.

Entrywise counit evaluation sends the localized generic matrix to the identity matrix, as required by the identity point in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). The proof checks diagonal and off-diagonal entries using the explicit counit formula. It works over every commutative base ring, and includes the empty matrix when n is zero. Checks pass: [counit_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L230), [counit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L294).
The counit gives the identity-matrix entry values.
Its determinant therefore evaluates to one.

Applying the antipode to each entry of the localized generic matrix produces its matrix inverse, the inversion operation described in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). This uses the already fixed order of coordinate indices. The determinant is a unit, so the formula describes genuine inversion rather than relying on Lean’s fallback value for a noninvertible matrix. Checks pass: [antipode_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L238), [antipode_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L300).
The antipode gives every corresponding inverse entry.
Its determinant becomes the inverse determinant.

The determinant has coproduct det(X)⊗det(X): taking determinants of the two-factor matrix product gives multiplicativity. This is the coordinate form of the determinant homomorphism GLₙ→Gₘ in [Stacks, determinant morphism](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022X). The tensor square is a unit because det(X) is a unit; no field, domain or positive-rank hypothesis is necessary. Checks pass: [map_comul_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L247), [counit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L294).
The coproduct matrix is the product of its tensor copies.
Identity evaluation gives the second group-like condition.

The localized determinant evaluates to one under the counit, because the counit sends the generic matrix to the identity and its determinant is one. This is preservation of the identity by the determinant homomorphism in [Stacks, determinant morphism](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022X). The empty determinant is also one, so the formula includes rank zero. Checks pass: [map_counit_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L261), [comul_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L277).
Counit evaluation gives the identity matrix.
The determinant also has the multiplicative coproduct formula.

The antipode sends det(X) to det(X)⁻¹, the inverse compatibility of the determinant morphism in [Stacks, determinant morphism](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022X). Lean writes Ring.inverse, which is zero on nonunits; here det(X) is explicitly a unit, so it denotes its genuine inverse. The proof takes the determinant of the actual inverse generic matrix. Checks pass: [map_antipode_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L268), [isUnit_det_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L113).
The antipode sends the matrix to its inverse.
The determinant is a unit, making Ring.inverse genuine.

The selected Hopf structure stores exactly the explicit localized matrix-multiplication coproduct of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). Lean displays heterogeneous equality because the stored module structure initially gives the linear maps differently presented types. Once that structure is selected, this is equality of the same map; it does not assert compatibility with an arbitrary alternative Hopf structure. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_comul_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L567), [coordinateHopfAlgebra_comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L597).
The bundled carrier transports this stored coproduct to the explicit map.
The resulting stored operation has the intended generator formula.

The selected Hopf structure stores the explicit counit evaluating at the identity matrix, as in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). The heterogeneous equality accounts for the stored module structure in the linear-map types. It records the actual selected map, not merely the existence of some counit on the same algebra or an equality for every possible structure. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_counit_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L578), [map_counit_genericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L634).
The bundle transports the stored counit to the explicit evaluation map.
That stored counit sends the generic matrix to the identity.

The selected Hopf structure stores precisely the explicit inverse-matrix antipode of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). Lean uses heterogeneous equality to identify linear maps whose types expose differently presented stored module structures. After those structures are selected, the maps agree directly. The statement fixes the chosen antipode rather than replacing it with an unrelated instance on the carrier. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_antipode_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L587), [map_antipode_genericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L657).
The bundled antipode transports to the explicit localized map.
It sends the bundled generic matrix to its actual inverse.

The bundled coproduct of a raw coordinate element equals its explicit localized coproduct transported into both bundled tensor factors. The algebra equivalence identifies the same carrier elements, while this equation checks the stored coalgebra operation. It therefore preserves the coordinate multiplication law of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51) on the entire localization, including determinant denominators. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L597), [map_comul_genericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L642).
Transport gives the explicit generator formula.
The stored map gives the product of bundled tensor-factor matrices.

The bundled antipode agrees with the raw inverse-matrix substitution after transporting the coordinate element through the canonical algebra equivalence. This checks the selected Hopf operation, which an algebra equivalence alone would not determine. The equation applies to every localized element and realizes the inversion map in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), including its action on determinant denominators. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_antipode_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L624), [map_antipode_genericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L657).
The transported map has the expected inverse-entry formula.
Its whole-matrix action is genuine inversion.

The stored coproduct on a bundled coordinate is ∑ₖxᵢₖ⊗xₖⱼ, with each variable transported into the bundled carrier. This verifies that bundling preserves the ordinary matrix-product convention in [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). The commutativity of the coordinate ring does not imply that its coproduct is symmetric or that GLₙ itself is commutative. Checks pass: [comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L220), [pointToGeneralLinear_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L183).
The raw localized map has the same ordered generator formula.
The stored coproduct produces ordinary multiplication of point matrices.

The stored counit evaluates a bundled generic coordinate to one on the diagonal and zero off the diagonal. Thus the chosen bundle retains the identity-point formula in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). This tests the actual coalgebra structure stored with the carrier, rather than inferring the counit solely from the underlying commutative algebra. Checks pass: [counit_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L230), [map_counit_genericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L634).
The raw counit has precisely these identity-entry values.
The stored entry formulas assemble into the identity matrix.

The stored antipode maps a bundled generic coordinate to the transported (i,j)-entry of the raw inverse matrix. This is the inversion formula in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51) with the same indices on both sides. Unit determinant ensures actual invertibility, and the separate inverse-transport equation identifies this with the inverse of the bundled generic matrix. Checks pass: [antipode_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L238), [genericMatrix_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L509).
The raw antipode has the matching inverse-entry formula.
The transported raw inverse entry equals the bundled inverse entry.

Forgetting the finite-generation certificate returns exactly the previously constructed coordinate Hopf algebra of GLₙ. The finite-type package adds a property, without replacing its carrier or Hopf operations. In the presentation of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), finite type means generation by finitely many coordinate elements and a determinant inverse, not finite cardinality or finite module rank. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L597), [adjoin_coordinateHopfAlgebra_X_union_antipode_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L701).
The underlying object retains its matrix coproduct.
Entries and inverse entries give a finite algebra-generating family.

A normed field carries a multiplicative absolute value, with distance determined by the norm of a difference. The metric laws supply the triangle inequality and ensure that only zero has norm zero. Neither completeness nor a nontrivial absolute value is required; the trivial absolute value is allowed. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L155).

A normed division ring has a multiplicative norm; its multiplication need not commute. The norm is exactly multiplicative and induces a genuine metric, so it separates zero from nonzero elements. Completeness is not assumed, and division means multiplication on the right by the inverse of the denominator. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L41).

A nontrivially normed field has an element of norm greater than one; its inverse has norm below one and contracting positive powers. The explanatory phrase “powers of any element” is too broad: powers of 1 do not contract. This wording slip does not change the standard mathematical definition. Compared with [Conrad, Norms Theorem2.1](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivnorms.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L167).

Dense norm values mean that every nonempty open interval in the nonnegative reals contains the norm of some field element. This implies nontriviality but is stronger than having arbitrarily small nonzero norms. Discrete p-adic norm values illustrate the distinction. The condition requires density, not attainment of every nonnegative real value. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 pp10–11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L174).

Scalar multiplication scales vector length by the scalar’s absolute value. Although Lean’s definition states only an inequality, applying it to inverse scalars gives equality. The vector length may be a seminorm, so nonzero vectors can have length zero. Neither completeness nor nontriviality of the scalar norm is required. Compared with [Conrad, Norms §1](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivnorms.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean#L37).

A normed algebra is a unital algebra with a seminorm compatible with scalar multiplication and submultiplicative in products. Multiplication in the algebra may be noncommutative, while scalars act centrally. Completeness, separation by the seminorm, and the normalization that the unit has norm one are not required. Compared with [Schweigert, Definition1.1.7](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean#L271).

Taking an inverse takes the reciprocal of the norm. The familiar identity for nonzero elements extends here to zero because both the division-ring inverse of zero and the real reciprocal of zero are defined as zero. The result allows noncommutative division rings and assumes no completeness. Compared with [Klazar, Exercise23](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L78).

The norm of a quotient is the quotient of the two norms. Division uses the right inverse of the denominator, even in a noncommutative division ring. No nonzero-denominator hypothesis is needed here: division by zero is defined as zero in both the division ring and the real numbers. Compared with [Klazar, Exercise23](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L70).

Norms commute with every integer power, including negative exponents. Negative powers use inverses, with the convention that zero to a negative integer power is zero. The zeroth power is one, even at zero. Thus the identity applies without excluding zero and does not require commutative multiplication. Compared with [Klazar, Exercise23](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L89).

For two nonzero elements, the distance between their inverses equals their original distance divided by the product of their norms. Both nonzero assumptions matter: the formula can fail when one element is zero. Factoring the difference of inverses proves the identity even when multiplication is noncommutative. Compared with [Klazar, Exercises23–24](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L96).

A nontrivially normed field contains an element whose norm is strictly greater than one. This exposes the extra assumption in the class, rather than asserting it for every normed field. A field with the trivial absolute value would fail this conclusion, although it still has distinct zero and one. Compared with [Conrad, Norms Theorem2.1](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivnorms.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L206).

There is a nonzero field element whose norm lies strictly between zero and one. Inverting an element with norm greater than one supplies such a witness. This depends on a nontrivial absolute value, not just a nonzero field, and does not assert that every small positive norm is attained. Compared with [Conrad, Norms Theorem2.1](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivnorms.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L239).

Norms in a nontrivially normed field are unbounded above: for every real bound, some field element has larger norm. Positive powers of one element with norm greater than one suffice. The bound may be negative, and the conclusion requires neither completeness nor density of the norm values. Compared with [Conrad, Norms Theorem2.1](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivnorms.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L214).

For every positive real bound, a nontrivially normed field contains a nonzero element of smaller norm. Inverting an element with sufficiently large norm proves this. The positivity of the bound is essential, and the strict lower bound excludes zero as a vacuous witness; no completeness or density is assumed. Compared with [Conrad, Absolute Values §2](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivabsvalues.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L225).

The coefficient map into a normed algebra preserves norms when the algebra’s unit has norm one. That normalization is an explicit hypothesis: without it, the general formula includes a factor equal to the norm of the unit. The target may still carry a seminorm, and completeness is unnecessary. Compared with [Conrad, Norms §1](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivnorms.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean#L300).

A normed space over an extension field becomes a normed space over the smaller field by sending each scalar through the coefficient map before acting. The vector seminorm is unchanged. Compatibility of the field norms makes this work; neither a finite extension nor complete fields or vector spaces are required. Compared with [Schweigert, Lemma1.1.23](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean#L485).

Restriction of scalars also preserves a normed algebra: a scalar from the smaller field acts through its image in the extension field. The algebra multiplication and seminorm stay the same. The two field norms must be compatible, but no finite-dimensionality, completeness, or unit-norm normalization on the algebra is required. Compared with [Schweigert, Lemma1.1.23](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean#L529).

A linear map pulls the target seminorm back to its domain by assigning x the length of f(x). Linearity preserves the triangle inequality and scalar homogeneity. Injectivity is not required: vectors in the kernel may have length zero, so the result is deliberately a seminormed space rather than necessarily a separated one. Compared with [Conrad, Norms §1](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivnorms.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean#L190).

The whole space is unbounded when it contains a nonzero vector, has a genuine norm, and its scalar field has a nontrivial absolute value. Scaling that vector by elements of arbitrarily large norm proves the claim. Both nontriviality and separation matter; a zero space or zero seminorm would be bounded. Compared with [Conrad, Norms §§1–2](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/equivnorms.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean#L211).

In a nonzero real normed space, the open ball of nonnegative radius r has diameter 2r. Opposite points approaching the boundary give the supremum, although it need not be attained inside the ball. At radius zero the ball is empty and its diameter is defined as zero. Compared with [Faris §§6.1–6.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean#L126).

For any ideal I in a commutative Noetherian ring R, the inverse limit of R/Iⁿ is Noetherian. Lean uses exactly these compatible quotient families; Noetherianity supplies finite generation of I. Indexing starts at n=0, whose quotient is the zero ring. Neither separatedness of R nor properness of I is assumed. See [Stacks 0316](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0316) and [source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Noetherian.lean#L212). Checks: the [integer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Examples/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Noetherian.lean#L22) and [polynomial](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Examples/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Noetherian.lean#L25) completion examples pass; the [complete but nonnoetherian control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Examples/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Noetherian.lean#L32) passes. The [roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4adc7e3d0b68a8bb9974126e7411667cb533255f/TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpacesPartII/README.md#L727) separately assigns finite-precision comparisons to evaluation-map APIs; this review covers noetherianity.
